page: Microsoft Azure D64pls_v6 is a compute-focused instance within the Dplsv6 series, powered by ARM-based Microsoft Neoverse-N2 processors operating at 3.4 GHz. The instance provisions 64 dedicated physical cores without simultaneous multithreading, mapped directly to 64 vCPUs. System memory totals 128 GB, establishing a 2 GB per core ratio. Cache layout consists of 64 KB L1 data cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache per core, and a shared 128 MB L3 cache. Cryptographic operations are hardware accelerated via native AES extensions, while x86-specific SIMD instruction sets such as AVX are absent due to the ARM architecture.

Hardware configuration excludes local disk storage and GPU accelerators, relying entirely on remote network-attached block storage for persistence. Memory subsystem benchmarks show high throughput, achieving 465.6 GB/sec in large-block uncached reads and 203.97 GB/sec in writes. Multi-core throughput benchmarks place the instance in the top decile, highlighted by a Geekbench multi-core score of 23,430 and a Clang software compilation score of 65,458. Conversely, single-thread performance scores remain in the median range across Geekbench and stress-ng tests.

With a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM allocation, this server provides a high core density that maximizes CPU throughput relative to allocated memory. The absence of bundled local storage requires provisioning external storage volumes, which must be factored into the overall infrastructure design. The instance architecture is suited for parallelized compilation pipelines, containerized microservices, batch processing, static web serving, and distributed database nodes where multi-threaded CPU execution and high memory bandwidth are prioritized over large per-core memory capacities.
description: Microsoft Azure D64pls_v6 is an ARM-based instance built on 64 dedicated Microsoft Neoverse-N2 physical cores running at 3.4 GHz, paired with 128 GB of RAM. The instance features a 2 GB per vCPU ratio, 128 MB of L3 cache, and dedicated single-thread execution per core without multithreading. It excludes local NVMe storage and discrete GPUs, operating entirely on remote storage. In synthetic and realistic benchmarks, the server delivers high multi-threaded compute performance and memory bandwidth, reflected in strong Clang compilation and multi-core execution metrics, while single-core metrics remain at median levels. This configuration offers high compute density suited for parallel workloads such as continuous integration build fleets, distributed caching, web serving, and scalable container environments.
